name: A Letter Undelivered
summary: A faded, bloodstained letter to Yvette Farthing lies among the skeletal ruins of Agamand Mills. It recalls two lovers parted as the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, and what the Forsaken left behind when they traded life for undeath.

sections.title: A Message Lost in the Fall
sections.body: Thurman Agamand, eldest son of patriarch Gregor Agamand, wrote the message that never reached Yvette Farthing. When the Plague of Undeath consumed Tirisfal Glades, Thurman refused to leave his ancestral home or his kin. As the Scourge struck, he took up his quill to write to Yvette, whom he had loved before the kingdom turned to ash.

sections.title: The Severed Bond
sections.body: When Yvette Farthing receives the letter at the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, a painful memory returns. She recalls begging Thurman to flee Agamand Mills with her and her father, and says his brother Brand bore him ill will. The warmth soon passes. Yvette steels her heart, casts aside mortal remorse, and declares that love has no place in her new existence.

faq.answer: Thurman Agamand, eldest son of Gregor Agamand, wrote the letter. He perished defending his family's mills against the Scourge alongside the rest of his cursed household.
Yvette Farthing is a Forsaken woman living inside the tavern in Brill. In life, she begged her lover Thurman Agamand to leave Agamand Mills with her and her father, but he stayed with his family.

faq.q: Where did the letter come from?
faq.answer: The letter is found among walking skeletons prowling the devastated grounds and fields of Agamand Mills in western Tirisfal Glades.

faq.q: What happened between Thurman and Yvette?
faq.answer: Thurman and Yvette were lovers before the Third War. She begged him to leave his family's mills and escape with her, but he stayed with his kin to face the Plague.

faq.q: What does Yvette do when she reads the letter?
faq.answer: Yvette briefly grieves for Thurman and curses both the Scourge and his brother Brand, then quickly suppresses her feelings. She says regrets are for the weak and romance has no place in her Forsaken existence.
Brand was Thurman Agamand's brother. Yvette says Brand harbored deep resentment and ill intent toward Thurman even before the estate fell to the Plague.

angles.text: The letter shows the painful divide between a Forsaken's mortal memories and the cold, purpose-driven existence they lead under the Banshee Queen.
For travelers in Brill, this recovered parchment shows the emotional detachment that defines the Forsaken people.
